focus: Spec-track narrowing: the repeat, the power, and the keep rule
noveltyJustification: The repeat's full record, the exact power numbers, the probability-aware reversal against the 017 corpus, and the landed 049 trust upgrades are new; the corpus/label critique carries forward from prior research with new evidence.
keyQuestions: Q2: spec-track narrowing proof, power, hardening, integration, tests
answeredQuestions: Q2: Spec-track narrowing (`score-track-narrowing.mjs`): given the repeat on 270 rows stopped on margin (106 vs 82, bootstrap interval spanning zero), what corpus, labels, keep rule and power would prove a live win or settle a kill; what question, option or input changes improve accuracy; which failure modes need hardening; where would it plug into a live path; what tests would cover it?
ruledOut: Reading the repeat as a kill (CI spans zero, underpowered)
Adopting probability-aware aggregation as a free row (lost 4 rows on the repeat)

label: The 017 keep did not repeat: the 270-row repeat printed stop (margin) K=270 M=270 A=106 B=82 W=80 L=56 F=48 p=0.02409 with bootstrap accuracy_delta_95_ci=[-0.1185,0.2760] clusters=16; the margin gate needed 27 rows and the gain was 24, while the sign test passed. The baseline rose 68/256 to 82/270 and Jev 97/256 to 106/270. The repeat is inconclusive, not a kill.

Exact binomial power against the margin gate: at the repeat's observed decided-pair win rate 0.588 (80 of 136), 80% power needs 217 decided pairs (~431 rows at the current 50.4% decided rate); at the current 136 decided pairs the MDE is 0.634 (~37 rows / 13.7pp); the repeat as run had 0.399 power at its own effect. A pre-registered power line (n, alpha, MDE) belongs in the report before a third run is read as decisive.
sources: computed: exact binomial tail sum P(2W-n_d>=27), W~Bin(n_d,0.588)

label: The frozen keep rule is relative-only (coverage 10*M>=9*K, margin 10*(A-B)>=M, sign test p<0.05, flips 10*F<=3*M) with no absolute accuracy floor and no per-track floor; A=106/270 (39.3%) would keep if the margin passed. Proving a live win needs operator-set absolute and per-track recall floors.

Probability-aware aggregation did not repeat its 017 gain: on the repeat it scored A=102 vs the modal 106 (decided-subset 102/203=0.5025, margin slack -7.0 rows, p=0.05018); the one-call arm scored 103. The three-order protocol buys stability, not accuracy, and the free-row claim is corpus-dependent; the shortlist arm remains unmeasured.

The 049 trust upgrades landed and show in the repeat record: rowSetSha256 + per-row questionSha256 + optionSetSha256 and the model tuple {jev 0.6.2, official, jev-1.13.0} are pinned; --out reuse is refused; --replay scores exactly the recorded rows and reports drops; the cluster bootstrap (16 clusters, 1000 replicates) runs in-report. The remaining trust gap is labels and population, not instrumentation.

Transfer warning persists and clusters are heterogeneous: paraphrase probes favor ripgrep 9/14 to Jev 2/14; per-track accuracy ranges from sk-git 14/19 to sk-design 3/20 (16 of 20 abstained); total abstained=55 (20.4%), with three tracks holding 31 of them. Any live path must be miss-only with fail-open, and sk-design-like clusters need description diagnosis first.

Cost is latency: p50 325 ms and p95 389 ms per call over 852 planned calls per arm, ~953,885 estimated input tokens (mostly the 17-option block); the one-call arm is within 3 rows of the modal arm (103 vs 106). A live path should serve one call on ambiguous/miss rows only inside a few-hundred-ms budget, keeping three orders offline.

Integration shape: add 'track-narrowing' with env JEV_FEATURE_TRACK_NARROWING to FEATURES and a Gate 1 advisory call site at lookup-trigger-index.mjs:132 that asks featureReady only when the lexical lookup misses or ties, prints an advisory, and fails open to broad search (the cite-drift advisory shape). Prior R1 (keep hard narrowing offline until a real-request holdout passes) is unchanged and strengthened by the repeat.
